detail.abstract: In this paper, I evaluate the impact of COVID-era asset purchase programs (APPs) on the dollar exchange rate in both emerging markets (EMs) and ex-US advanced economies (AEs). In an event study analysis that includes APP announcements for 23 EMs and seven AEs, I find that APPs appreciated the exchange rate in EMs after controlling for the policy actions of the Federal Reserve (Fed), including the Fed swap lines, the policy actions of other AEs, and the simultaneous policy actions of the implementing country itself. I interpret the results through the lens of long-run uncovered interest rate parity deviations driven by sovereign credit risk, showing that asset purchase surprises lower the promised yield but do not necessarily decrease the underlying risk-free rate in EMs. These results suggest that APPs might help EMs stabilize exchange rates during episodes of distress without necessarily intervening in the foreign exchange market.

detail.title: A Novel Incremental Lp-norm Regulated Kernel-free Forecasting Method Based on Support Vectors
detail.abstract: In the big data era, real-life datasets often consist of data streams that represent varying trends over time. The influx of massive data points within short-time intervals presents significant challenges for optimal decision-making, particularly in real-time big data analysis. In the context of nonlinear forecasting, it becomes essential to reduce the reliance on history data and efficiently update regression coefficients to accommodate newly-inflowed data. To address this, we propose a novel incremental nonlinear forecasting method, the Incremental Lp-norm Regulated Least Squares Regression method based on Support Vectors (ILpLSR-SV). This method combines kernel-free support vector regression (SVR) with Lp-norm regularization to efficiently handle nonlinear regression by directly using a quadratic surface. The Lp-norm regularization (where p ∈ (0, 1)) is applied to all single and quadratic features to reduce the impact of redundant features, leading to a sparse solution. To enable efficient incremental forecasting, we introduce an adaptive pruning algorithm to select the most relevant support vectors and propose an implementing algorithm to find an ϵ-KKT point of the ILpLSR-SV model, with a worst-case complexity analysis. Extensive experiments on public time-series and benchmark datasets demonstrate that the ILpLSR-SV method outperforms existing incremental forecasting methods in terms of forecasting accuracy, particularly on time-series datasets. Moreover, the proposed method exhibits significant computational efficiency during the training phase, especially when dealing with newly-inflowed data streams. These results highlight IL p LSR-SVs strong potential for real-life, large-scale forecasting applications with massive data streaming in the big data era.

detail.title: Accounting for the Patterns of Invoicing Currency in Global Trade
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the determinants of international trade invoicing by quantifying the relative importance of structural relationships, global currency dynamics, and country-specific developments. Using a comprehensive dataset for 132 countries from 1990-2024 that includes the US dollar, the euro, and the Chinese renminbi, a multi-dimensional fixed effects model is used to disentangle these three forces. A subsequent variance decomposition analysis is further used to assess their relative explanatory power. The empirical results suggest that invoicing patterns are overwhelmingly determined by time-invariant, country-currency specific structural factors, which explain approximately 60% of the total variation. Global, currency-specific trends account for another 30%, while idiosyncratic, country-specific developments have a surprisingly minimal impact, explaining less than 10%. Our results reveal a global invoicing system characterized by immense inertia, suggesting that national policies are largely ineffective in altering invoicing behavior without fundamentally changing a country’s deep-seated integration into the global trade and financial network. Important policy suggestions follow.

title: Junior Golf: Examining the Economic Reality of Seeking a Scholarship

detail.title: Junior Golf: Examining the Economic Reality of Seeking a Scholarship
detail.abstract: Junior golf represents one of the most financially demanding youth sports in America, with families often investing between $150,000 and $300,000 over a 13-year period. Yet the potential return-college golf scholarships-is limited and unevenly distributed: only 13.2% of top-ranked boys and 51.0% of top-ranked girls receive any Division I or II athletic aid. This study investigates whether junior golf functions as a viable financial investment or an expensive gamble, drawing on national data, scholarship statistics, and personal case studies. Through detailed cost breakdowns, comparative scholarship analysis, and peer investment profiles, this research reveals a significant economic mismatch between money spent and money earned through college funding. While the vast majority of junior golfers will never recoup their investment, this paper argues that financial return should not be the primary justification for participation. Instead, the real value of junior golf lies in the development of life skills, character, and networking opportunities that extend far beyond scholarship dollars. Ultimately, junior golf offers meaningful long-term benefits-but not necessarily financial ones-making honest expectation setting essential for families navigating this costly pursuit.

detail.abstract:
Purpose-Estimates disclosure of human capital management for Chinese listed companies. Investigate the patterns of the disclosure of human capital management across industries and regions. Examine the determinants of human capital management disclosure in China. Examine the association between human capital management disclosure and firm performance. 

Design/methodology/approach-We employ natural language processing techniques on annual reports' management discussion and analysis sections. We construct exposure measures for ten human capital management dimensions and synthesize them into one comprehensive measure of human capital management disclosure. We conduct empirical analysis on the measure using a sample of Chinese listed companies during 2009-2022. 

Findings-We construct a measure of human capital management disclosure for 5,153 Chinese companies during 2009-2022. We find that firms with high HCM disclosure are more labor intensive and have more cash holdings and R&D expenditure but have lower sales growth, market-to-book ratio and leverage. HCM disclosure is associated with better future accounting performance but poor future market valuation. There are substantial variations in HCM disclosure across industries, geographic regions and ownership types. HCM disclosure has increased significantly during the COVID-19 pandemic. 

Social implications-The increased HCM disclosure and its association with firm operating performance and market valuation indicate the relevance of HCM in corporate management and underscore the need for more robust and standardized disclosure of HCM in China. Our findings support recent regulatory efforts by CSRC to enhance the transparency and accountability in HCM disclosures and advocate for more explicit and specific HCM disclosure requirements in the future. 

Originality/value-We propose a quantitative measure of human capital management disclosure, which can be modified to apply to other markets. We construct a comprehensive, ready-to-use dataset for HCM disclosure for Chinese listed companies and conduct descriptive analysis on the dataset. We identify the patterns of human capital management disclosure and its determinants in China.

publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
In a  previous post, we provided background information about the emergence of tokenized investment funds and their use cases. These use cases are currently limited to the digital asset ecosystem. However, the recent approval of cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and the passage of the GENIUS Act raise concerns about the impact of these tokenized investment fund to the broader financial system. In this post, we assess this impact by considering three economic mechanisms based in part on market participants’ investment strategies and liquidity needs. They include: liquidity transformation, interconnections between the digital asset and the traditional financial system, and transaction settlement. Through these mechanisms, tokenization of investment funds can bring about financial stability benefits in the form of reduced redemption pressures and additional sources of liquidity for fund issuances, but may also increase interconnectedness between the traditional financial system and digital asset ecosystem, thereby amplifying existing financial stability risks.

detail.abstract: This study explores the positive roles of youths in building social cohesion in Bulchana Woreda of Shashemene city, west Arsi zone, Oromia national regional state, Ethiopia. While much of existing literatures and media narratives predominantly associate youth with conflict, violence, and political unrest in Ethiopia, this research highlights their constructive contributions beyond conventional peace building, encompassing broader dimensions of social cohesion. Drawing on Kearns and Forrest's (2000) integral framework, the study investigated youths' voluntary engagement in fostering civic culture, social order, social solidarity, social networks, and place attachment within their community. A qualitative ethnographic research design was employed. Data were collected through indepth interviews, focus group discussions, and nonparticipant observations, and analyzed thematically. The findings reveal that youths actively participate in voluntary initiatives such as feeding programs for the vulnerable, renew house for the helpless, and promote peace through cultural events, environmental campaigns, voluntary teaching, and awareness rising on civic duties and public health. These actions enhanced mutual care, trust, and interdependence in the community. The study also identified key social generative factors including communal solidarity, moral values of care, youth solidarity networks, and institutional partnerships that fostered youths' involvement. However, their efforts faced a challenges such as lack of sustained institutional support, youth unemployment, ethnic and political divisions, distrust from authorities, and gender based exclusion. The study recommends that local government and stakeholders should recognize and strengthen youths' positive roles through sustained funding, inclusive policies, and capacity building programs, positioning them as agents of social generativity and sustainable peace.

detail.abstract: We characterize Nash equilibria in multi-product markets in which producers commit to vectors of supply functions contingent on all prices. The framework accommodates (dis)economies of scope in production, and goods may be substitutes or complements in demand. We show that equilibrium allocations of underlying goods and payoffs are invariant under bundling. With quadratic costs and linear demand, this invariance reduces the multi-product problem to an equivalent set of single-product markets that can be analyzed independently. We introduce Lerner and pass-through matrices to capture markups and welfare losses; their eigenvalues summarize fundamental market properties, remain invariant under bundling, and lend themselves to comparative statics analysis.

detail.title: Foreign Direct Investment, Tourism Infrastructure, and the Labor Market As Channels of the Maldives’s Economic Integration with the Global Economy
detail.abstract: This study investigates the role of foreign direct investment (FDI), tourism infrastructure, and the labor market as channels of the Maldives's economic integration with the global economy. Given the country's structural reliance on tourism and services, these three dimensions represent critical interfaces through which external linkages shape domestic development. The analysis is based exclusively on empirical methods, drawing from national statistics, international databases, and sectoral reports. FDI flows are examined in relation to resort development and supporting services, while tourism infrastructure indicators-such as hotel capacity, transport facilities, and energy supply-are analyzed for their contribution to international competitiveness. The labor market dimension highlights the significance of both foreign workers and skill development in shaping the adaptability of the Maldivian economy. Results show that these channels collectively reinforce the Maldives's global integration, though with uneven benefits and persistent vulnerabilities, underscoring the need for policies that balance openness with resilience.

detail.title: Data Technology Empowerment and Corporate Green Innovation
detail.abstract: Data, emerging as a new key factor of production following land, capital, labor, and technology, is profoundly transforming firms’ operating models and innovation paradigms. However, it remains unclear whether leveraging data can help firms fulfill their corporate social responsibility and mitigate environmental externalities. This paper investigates the effect of data technology utilization on corporate green innovation. Using a sample of Chinese non-financial listed firms from 2010 to 2023, we find strong and robust evidence that data technology utilization significantly improves the quality of firms’ green patent portfolios. The effect is more pronounced for pollution-heavy firms, non-state-owned enterprises, and firms in provinces with stronger intellectual property protection. Mechanism tests show that the utilization of data technologies enhances green innovation quality by enabling more informed decision-making and more efficient resource allocation. Overall, our findings demonstrate the important role of data-driven technologies in promoting environmentally sustainable growth in the digital economy era.

detail.abstract: Trade security is a pivotal element in turbulent times. The new megaregional treaty between Mercosur and the EU will set a geopolitical milestone for better trade and global food security in a world of turmoil. Add Ukraine as another major player despite the aggression from Russia, and you get a new “default” food treaty picture looking like a somewhat strange triangle between three food giants. Given the many sensitivities especially in Europe, there can be no free lunch with a full glass of free food trade: all menu recipes – including new and especially powerful agricultural safeguards - are still concocted in Brussels, instead of based on fully reciprocal concessions and lobal standards. Moreover, only the EU will have treaties with the other two giants, and with countless other countries. Nevertheless, the European Commission rightly calls the treaty with Mercosur a ‘groundbreaking’ partnership agreement for Europe’s economy. It also promises EU farmers more exports and only minimally increasing imports. This Working Paper asks three questions on (i) the recognition of defensive food import interests, (ii) the treatment of specifically European environmental and social concerns, and (iii) Ukraine’s EU market access guarantees under rapidly evolving preferential terms. To heap more problems on this conundrum, WTO compatibility questions and market share expectations of competitive agrifood behemoths enjoying new preferences throw a light on the residual value of EU concessions agreed earlier under WTO and other RTA. Perhaps a WTO silver bullet like the one solving the infamous banana dispute can help finding a legal win-win solution for all food value chain participants?

detail.title: A Blockwise Approach for Testing the Stability of Conditional Probability Equivalent Level of VaR and ES

declarations.funderStatement: Yanxi Hou’s work was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China Grants 72171055 and 71991471.

detail.abstract: The Probability Equivalent Level of VaR and ES (PELVE), introduced by Li & Wang (2023), serves as a distributional index that quantifies the change in risk level when transitioning from Value-at-Risk (VaR) to Expected Shortfall (ES). Developing feasible methods to evaluate PELVE holds both theoretical and practical significance. This paper proposes a blockwise scheme to test the stability of PELVE and dual PELVE within the framework of an ARMA-GARCH model. Specifically, we employ a self-weighted quasi maximum likelihood estimation for parameter estimation, which enables us to obtain empirical PELVE and dual PELVE using the residuals process. We then compare the blockwise empirical PELVE and dual PELVE with their full-sample counterparts using Kolmogorov-Smirnov-type and Cramér-von-Mises-type test statistics. Additionally, we establish the asymptotic properties of these tests and bootstrap the critical values using a blockwise method. A simulation study validates our theoretical findings in finite samples. An empirical application to S&P 500 Indices data further demonstrates the effectiveness of our tests.

keywords: EPA Rules To Curb Methane Emissions

detail.abstract: While much evidence identifies the human and environmental impacts of excessive methane gas (CH4) emissions, climate scientists and world bodies have yet to explore whether financial markets price these impacts. Financial markets play an important role in reducing global warming because investors can penalize emitter firms today as a reduction in market value for the costs of their future emissions. Using firmlevel data on industrial CH4 and CO2 emissions mandatorily reported to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), we document five key findings. First, the equity market penalizes firms for high levels of CH4 by imposing a share price discount that is at least six times higher than the share price discount for CO2. Second, this discrepancy arguably reflects investors' use of a higher global warming factor for CH4 than the one used by the EPA. Third, the CH4 valuation discount is largely driven by industry-level rather than firm-specific emissions. Fourth, the market penalty is stronger for firms in Blue states, those with limited CH4 disclosure in 10-K filings, and those with limited media mentions, suggesting that investors' negative response to CH4 is more severe when climate regulation is stricter and disclosure transparency weaker. Fifth, we examined two regulations, finding that (i) firms located in states supporting the 2016 EPA methane regulations to reduce emissions face a sharper market penalty after the rules were later overturned by a federal court; and (ii) firms headquartered in states required to disclose harmful chemicals used in hydraulic fracturing experience a smaller market penalty.

detail.title: Navigating the green path: unveiling the financial impact of green management
detail.abstract: This study explores how green management practices influence corporate financial performance using a panel of 12,503 firm-year observations from 48 countries. We find that stronger green management is significantly associated with higher profitability, with a one-standard-deviation increase linked to a 4.87 percentage point rise in return on assets (ROA). To mitigate endogeneity concerns, we employ an instrumental variable approach using country-level carbon regulations. The financial benefits of green management are more pronounced in low carbon-intensive sectors and high-income countries, and comparatively weaker in high carbon-intensive sectors and middle-income economies. While green management enhances operational efficiency, its negative association with Tobin’s Q suggests that investor perceptions and market dynamics may limit the market’s recognition of its broader benefits. Overall, these findings highlight the strategic value of green management for financial success and offer valuable insights for corporate decision-makers and policymakers navigating the transition to sustainable business practices.

title: European Industrial Policy: A Challenge and a Chance for Competition Policy

detail.title: European Industrial Policy: A Challenge and a Chance for Competition Policy
detail.abstract: This paper examines the evolving relationship between industrial policy and competition law enforcement in Europe. It argues that while competition policy was long regarded as the gcornerstone of economic growth and efficiency, the unintended and unanticipated costs of goblalization revealed during the 2008 financial crisis and the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic, the rising market concentration and profit margins, and the challenges of regulating the digital economy through competition law instruments—have led to a renewed embrace of industrial policy and a shift of societal goals toward innovation, resilience and strategic independence. The paper then examines the gradual development of industrial policy in Europe in the 21st century and analyzes, in the light of past experiences, the main safeguards  which would be necessary to ensure that European industrial policy is implemented in a way that preserves firms’ incentives to innovate and compete. The paper then analyzes how competition law should evolve from a static, short-term price efficiency focus toward a more dynamic framework incorporating the goals of innovation, sustainability, and resilience. The paper concludes that industrial policy and competition enforcement, far from having to be antagonistic, must and can complement and reinforce each other in the pursuit of the new societal goals without losing sight of their respective logic. Adapting to these changing circumstances is a challenge which must be met by competition authorities if they want to keep their independence but also a chance to remain relevant.

detail.abstract: We study the problem of optimal liquidity withdrawal for a representative liquidity provider (LP) in an automated market maker (AMM). LPs earn fees from trading activity but are exposed to impermanent loss (IL) due to price fluctuations. While existing work has focused on static provision and exogenous exit strategies, we characterise the optimal exit time as the solution to a stochastic control problem with an endogenous stopping time. Mathematically, the LP's value function is shown to satisfy a Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman quasi-variational inequality, for which we establish uniqueness in the viscosity sense. To solve the problem numerically, we develop two complementary approaches: a Euler scheme based on operator splitting and a Longstaff-Schwartz regression method. Calibrated simulations highlight how the LP's optimal exit strategy depends on the oracle price volatility, fee levels, and the behaviour of arbitrageurs and noise traders. Our results show that while arbitrage generates both fees and IL, the LP's optimal decision balances these opposing effects based on the pool state variables and price misalignments. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of dynamic liquidity provision in AMMs and provides insights into the sustainability of passive LP strategies under different market regimes.

detail.abstract: Emotional competence, including regulation, empathy, and self-control, is a critical developmental asset in adolescence, influencing psychological well-being and academic success. Social support-particularly from family, school, and peers-is thought to play a key role in developing these emotional skills, but cultural differences in educational values and social structures may influence these associations. This study examined how perceived social support from family, school, and peers relates to adolescent emotional competence in two culturally distinct nations: Slovakia (individualistic) and China (collectivist). A cross-sectional survey was administered to 268 adolescents in Slovakia and 253 in China from10 to 15 years old. Emotional competence and social support were measured using validated scales. We used Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) to examine associations between support sources and emotional competence domains in each country. In Slovakia, all three sources of support significantly predicted emotional regulation; peer and school support linked to empathy; and family and school support were associated with self-control. In China, family and peer support predicted emotional regulation; peer support was the sole predictor of empathy; and all three support sources were linked to self-control. Notably, peer support had a stronger influence on all social competence capabilities in China than in Slovakia. The influence of social support on adolescent emotional competence varies across cultural contexts. School support plays a more prominent role in Slovakia, while peer support has greater influence in China. These findings underscore the importance of culturally tailored interventions to foster emotional development in adolescence.

declarations.funderStatement: This work used the Dutch national e-infrastructure with the support of the SURF Cooperative using grant no. EINF-7774.

detail.abstract:
Problem Definition: In attended home delivery services, fast and accurate estimation of marginal routing costs is essential for time slot management. These costs determine the impact of each customer's time slot choice on overall routing efficiency, and must be computed in real-time as customers make bookings. Accurately estimating this costs is challenging, and requires striking a balance between computational efficiency and precision.

Methodology/results: This paper presents a novel hybrid approach that combines operations research (OR) heuristics with supervised machine learning (ML) to estimate these costs in real-time. Through extensive simulations, we compare the performance of a wide range of methods, both on the final resulting routing costs and on required evaluation time, given the real-time nature of this problem. We show that the hybrid variants consistently outperform their pure OR counterparts, with only a moderate impact on evaluation time. We also evaluate the impact of incorporating future demand scenarios, and find that doing so leads to further improvements in final route length, again with a reasonable computational trade-off.

Implications: These results suggest that meaningful cost savings can be achieved through simple, structured learning models and scenario-based reasoning, without sacrificing responsiveness. The proposed methods are practical and fast enough to be deployed in real-time systems, making them relevant for both researchers and practitioners working on operational decision-making in periodic attended home delivery.

detail.abstract: As bearings are critical mechanical components, their actual operating conditions exhibit notable dynamic complexity. Multiple factors-including rotational speed fluctuations, sudden load changes, and environmental disturbances-interact in a strongly coupled fashion. This imposes severe challenges on traditional fault diagnosis methods, such as limited interpretability, weak adaptive capacity, and elevated misjudgment rates. Therefore, this paper proposes an Interval Belief Rule Base model integrated with an attention mechanism (IBRB-a) under variable operating conditions. The proposed model combines expert knowledge's ability to quantify uncertainty with a data-driven adaptation mechanism, thereby addressing the challenge of variable operating conditions in complex industrial systems. First, a novel interval rule construction method is incorporated into the traditional IBRB model, and kernel density estimation (KDE) is employed to select reference values. Second, during the model reasoning process, a two-stage fusion strategy based on ER is adopted: progressive information fusion is implemented via the ER analysis algorithm and the ER rule algorithm, which effectively mitigates the interval uncertainty under variable operating conditions. Finally, the constrained projected covariance matrix adaptive evolution strategy (P-CMA-ES) is employed to optimize the model. Furthermore, experimental validation under variable operating conditions is conducted via Case Western Reserve University and Southeast University bearing dataset. The effectiveness and generalizability of the proposed method are validated by the experimental result

detail.abstract: This paper examines China’s evolving role in global climate governance within the context of a shifting world order. As the United States retreats from multilateral leadership, China has emerged as the world’s largest builder of renewable energy, the dominant actor in clean technology supply chains, and an increasingly central player in international climate diplomacy. Drawing on hegemonic transition theory, complex interdependence, and constructivist norm diffusion, the paper situates China’s climate leadership within broader structural and normative transformations. Empirical evidence highlights both China’s extraordinary renewable energy expansion and market dominance, as well as the contradictions of its continued reliance on coal and uneven emissions trajectory. The analysis critiques prevailing narratives that portray China either as a “green savior” or a “coal villain,” arguing that such framings obscure the dual-track and contested nature of its leadership. The paper concludes that China’s role should be understood not as the ascension of a new climate hegemon, but as part of a multipolar and interdependent process of climate governance in which shared responsibility, South–South cooperation, and normative contestation are as significant as material power.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how natural disasters affect firm credit in Mexico during eight years when an emergency, full-coverage guarantee program was repeatedly activated. Using loan-level data, we find that disaster declarations increase guaranteed credit exclusively through program-eligible loans. These loans exhibit modest size increases but significantly lower interest rates and longer maturities, particularly for new firm-bank relationships. While unsecured lending remains largely unaffected, it increases in municipalities without program coverage. New lending relationships form only through eligible guaranteed credit, with new borrowers partially reallocated from ineligible loans. This limited extensive-margin effect reveals missed opportunities for financial inclusion, as new program borrowers show similar retention rates to non-program borrowers. We find no evidence of higher default rates under the program, indicating that welltargeted full-coverage guarantees do not encourage excessive risk-taking. Our results highlight the value of guarantees for improving post-disaster loan terms as well as the potential for more flexible schemes with graduated coverage rates to broaden access while controlling fiscal costs.

title: Simplifying physical risk adaption for banks in the EU
affiliations: I am currently a Visiting Senior Fellow at the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE). and European Central Bank (ECB)

detail.title: Simplifying physical risk adaption for banks in the EU
detail.abstract: In this paper, we study the effectiviness of the two channels in which the financial system contributes to physical risks adaptation in the EU as per the NGFS (2024).  First, we assess the effectiveness of the level 3 prudential regulations on encouraging banks to include  adaptation in their risk management and client engagement. Our analysis takes a broad perspective, encompassing not only prudential risk management but also transparency regulation.  We deem the latter most relevant to the extent that stakeholders can incentivize adaptation.  Secondly, we examine how banks finance adaptation and the factors that enable this process, drawing on recent financial literature. Our findings indicate banks should integrate adaptation to physical risks into stress tests, transition plans, and Pillar III disclosures. Transition plans must address physical hazards, exposure, vulnerability, and set adaptation targets. Adaptation measures should be treated as risk mitigants, with their severity and consistency reflected in transition plans and stress tests. Green bonds and green loans can serve as effective private financing channels for adaptation.

title: The Stability Gap Model: A Structural Measure of Financial Fragility & Its Application in Portfolio Risk Management

detail.title: The Stability Gap Model: A Structural Measure of Financial Fragility & Its Application in Portfolio Risk Management
detail.abstract: Financial crises rarely erupt without warning; they are preceded by long periods of hidden fragility. Yet traditional market indicators such as the VIX capture only realized volatility, offering little foresight. This paper introduces the Stability Gap Model (SGM), developed iteratively from a simple intuition: fragility arises when risk-taking diverges from fundamentals and systemic buffers are insufficient. We trace the evolution of the model from its original formulation, through corrections and extensions, to its present form. The Classic SGM captures instantaneous imbalance, while the Beta SGM incorporates memory of past shocks. Empirical analysis demonstrates that the SGM provided clear early warnings ahead of the 2008 Global Financial Crisis, the 2011 Eurozone debt episode, the 2015 China/oil slowdown, and the 2018 tightening cycle, while also trending upward in 2019 before the COVID-19 crash. Furthermore, the paper demonstrates the model's utility in assessing fragility in hedge funds and proposes its application as a universal framework for stability analysis across diverse systems, from corporate finance to supply chains.

title: Electricity on Paper, Darkness in Practice: A Predictive Framework for India's Rural Energy Plans

detail.title: Electricity on Paper, Darkness in Practice: A Predictive Framework for India's Rural Energy Plans
detail.abstract:
Why Rural Electricity Projects Look Good on Paper But Fail in Real Life: A Study of India's Power Programs
India has achieved impressive results in bringing electricity to rural areas. Government data shows that by April 2018, all villages had electric connections. By March 2019, almost every household that wanted electricity got it through a program called Saubhagya. These numbers look very good on paper.

However, the reality is quite different. People in rural areas still face major problems. They experience power cuts that last 8-10 hours every day. The electrical systems are weak and unreliable. Many households have connections but cannot actually use electricity when they need it.

This creates what we call the "Paper vs Reality Problem"—when government programs seem successful in reports but fail to work properly for the people they are meant to help. Most research studies either look at how policies are designed OR study why they failed later. Very few studies connect these two parts. This research tries to fill that missing link.

Our study examined failed electricity projects in five Indian states: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu. We used a method called "Project Failure Analysis" to understand what went wrong. 

We organized these problems into a "Readiness Checklist" that gives scores for how prepared different areas are for new projects. We also created what we call the "Problem-Fighting System"—a way to help programs defend themselves against common issues that cause failure.

This research helps in two main ways. First, it explains the theory behind why some programs work while others fail. We call this the "Design-to-Results Connection." Second, it gives government officials a practical tool called the "Early Warning System" to spot potential problems before starting new projects.

Instead of waiting for programs to fail and then trying to fix them, this approach helps identify and solve problems beforehand. This could help India do a better job of making sure electricity programs actually improve people's lives, not just look good in government reports.

detail.abstract: The year 2025 brought a remarkable shift in the role of tariffs in the US economy, as the Trump administration simultaneously escalated the use of broad tariffs and ensured that Congress enacted large income tax cuts. This fiscal switch has important implications for the US tax system. While maintaining tariff rates at summer 2025 levels would generate large government revenues, such broad tariffs have significant downsides: Efficiency losses would approach one-third of revenues raised, the tax system would be less progressive, and there would be serious tax administration concerns. The fiscal shift also has significant macroeconomic implications, although probably not the intended ones. Broad tariffs generate a large negative supply shock, simultaneously raising prices and reducing macroeconomic activity.

title: The Gold Channel: How Regional Gold Saving Behavior Shapes House Price Dynamics in Türkiye
affiliations: Government of the Republic of Turkey - Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey and

detail.title: The Gold Channel: How Regional Gold Saving Behavior Shapes House Price Dynamics in Türkiye
detail.abstract: The last decade has seen growing demand for alternative assets, including non-fiat hedging instruments such as gold and cryptocurrencies. Widespread use of these unanchored assets poses challenges for policymakers due to their low monetary policy sensitivity and weak regulatory integration. While wealth effects of traditional assets such as real estate and equities have been studied extensively, the broader macroeconomic implications of alternative assets remain underexplored. In this paper, we analyze the wealth effects of gold on the housing market in Türkiye, an emerging market economy where households accumulate substantial gold savings, by using the global gold price rally in 2023 and 2024. Using a novel province level administrative dataset and exploiting the geographic heterogeneity in gold savings behavior, we implement a difference-indifferences strategy to show that increases in gold prices significantly elevate local house prices, particularly in provinces with higher gold savings. We estimate an average 10% cumulative additional increase in house prices attributable to the "gold channel". The effect operates through a liquidity-driven mechanism, as reflected by an increased share of cash-based housing transactions rather than credit-based ones, in contrast to traditional wealth channels. Importantly, we find that gold-induced wealth depresses the volumes in secondary market for houses. Instrumental variable analyses following Aiello et al. (2024) support the causal interpretation and clarify the mechanism. These results indicate the growing importance of accounting for the alternative saving instruments such as gold in asset price dynamics and macroeconomic transmission, particularly in inflationary environments.

detail.title: Enhanced Optimization of Nut Supply Chains using Metaheuristic Algorithms
detail.abstract: This study investigates the optimization of supply chains for nuts, focusing on the application of metaheuristic algorithms. We propose an enhanced approach using the Variable Neighborhood Search (VNS) algorithm and compare its performance against a Genetic Algorithm (GA) and an exact method. The results demonstrate that VNS outperforms GA in both computational efficiency and solution quality. While there is a slight trade-off in solution precision compared to the exact method, VNS significantly reduces computational time. This research contributes to the development of efficient optimization techniques for agricultural supply chains, addressing the complexities of resource management and distribution.

title: The Catholic Claim of Supremacy Over the Bible: A Prophetic and Historical Challenge

detail.title: The Catholic Claim of Supremacy Over the Bible: A Prophetic and Historical Challenge
detail.abstract:
This paper, The Catholic Claim of Supremacy Over the Bible: A Prophetic and Historical Challenge, examines the Roman Catholic Church’s long-standing assertion that its authority stands above Scripture. By tracing doctrinal claims, historical documents, and their devastating consequences, it demonstrates how this doctrine aligns with biblical prophecies of the Antichrist spirit and has produced centuries of oppression, colonization, and spiritual deception—particularly against African and African American communities.

The work highlights three core dangers of this claim: (1) direct defiance of Scripture’s command not to alter God’s Word, (2) fulfillment of prophetic warnings concerning a power that would change times and laws, and (3) the historical fruit of slavery, colonization, and systemic injustice enabled under religious sanction. It further explores the enduring effects on the Black church, including cultural erasure, systemic poverty, drug epidemics, police abuse, and spiritual confusion.

Finally, the paper calls for a prophetic response: a return to Sola Scriptura—Scripture alone as the supreme authority—combined with repentance, discernment, and liberation through Christ. It argues that only by rejecting human traditions that exalt themselves over God’s Word can the church reclaim its true foundation and break cycles of bondage. This work stands as both academic witness and prophetic warning, preserving a voice of resistance and remembrance for the Remnant and future generations.

detail.abstract:
The Treasury and IRS have proposed well-thought-out cloud transaction sourcing rules that are sorely needed. They include relevant and appropriate allocation factors and have made reasonable judgments in balancing theoretical accuracy with administrative simplicity.

This article both refutes certain criticisms that have been made against these proposed sourcing rules and suggests important amendments that it is hoped will be implemented when these regulations are finalized in the future. These amendments include the requirement that sourcing results for multinationals be determined on a unitary approach, the mis-labeled the intangible property factor is renamed and adjusted, and the coverage of the proposed three-factor formula approach is expanded to include all income from services conducted through electronic mediums.

title: An Attention-enhanced Interval Belief Rule Base Method for Bearing Fault Diagnosis Under Variable_ Operating Conditions

detail.title: An Attention-enhanced Interval Belief Rule Base Method for Bearing Fault Diagnosis Under Variable_ Operating Conditions

keywords.keywords: Interval belief rule baseRolling bearing fault diagnosisCross-condition diagnosisGeneralization ability

detail.abstract: As bearings are critical mechanical components, their actual operating conditions exhibit notable dynamic complexity. Multiple factors-including rotational speed fluctuations, sudden load changes, and environmental disturbances-interact in a strongly coupled fashion. This imposes severe challenges on traditional fault diagnosis methods, such as limited interpretability, weak adaptive capacity, and elevated misjudgment rates. Therefore, this paper proposes an Interval Belief Rule Base model integrated with an attention mechanism (IBRB-a) under variable operating conditions. The proposed model combines expert knowledge's ability to quantify uncertainty with a data-driven adaptation mechanism, thereby addressing the challenge of variable operating conditions in complex industrial systems. First, a novel interval rule construction method is incorporated into the traditional IBRB model, and kernel density estimation (KDE) is employed to select reference values. Second, during the model reasoning process, a two-stage fusion strategy based on ER is adopted: progressive information fusion is implemented via the ER analysis algorithm and the ER rule algorithm, which effectively mitigates the interval uncertainty under variable operating conditions. Finally, the constrained projected covariance matrix adaptive evolution strategy (P-CMA-ES) is employed to optimize the model. Furthermore, experimental validation under variable operating conditions is conducted via Case Western Reserve University and Southeast University bearing dataset. The effectiveness and generalizability of the proposed method are validated by the experimental result

title: Disasters and Tightness of Social Norms: The Case of Female Genital Cutting
affiliations: Universidad de Alicante, University of Barcelona and Universidad Autónoma de Madrid

detail.title: Disasters and Tightness of Social Norms: The Case of Female Genital Cutting

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: We examine the empirical relationship between exposure to disasters and tightness of social norms, focusing on the practice of female genital cutting (FGC) in Sub-Saharan Africa. Social norms tightness refers to the extent to which cultural groups enforce adherence to norms and punish deviations. It is a key factor in shaping how societies function and individuals behave, influencing everything from social order and conflict to collective effort and institutional dynamics, and often emerges and evolves as an adaptive response to adverse events. Drawing on occurrences of epidemics and natural disasters, we find that individuals surveyed in the aftermath of a disaster in their region adhere 4 to 6 percent of a standard deviation more closely to the opinions about FGC in their groups compared to those interviewed just before the disaster occurred. This effect is particularly pronounced among women and rural populations. By examining variations in early life exposure to disasters across birth cohorts within countries, we find that this effect persists over time and is strongest when the disaster occurs during the transition from childhood to early adolescence.

title: AI Business Applications Training and Business Outcomes: An Inclusive Intervention for Underrepresented Entrepreneurs

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: This study investigates the associations between university-led training in AI business applications and business outcomes among small firms, with a focus on underrepresented entrepreneurs in England, Wales, and Scotland. A total of 121 non-native, disabled, and non-heterosexual entrepreneurs participated in a four-month training programme covering AI applications for communication, finance, project management, and other key business functions. Data were collected before the training (2023) and one year later (2024). Using panel data estimates, the findings indicate that, post-training, firms experienced an increase in digital competencies, which were positively associated with customer satisfaction, entrepreneurs' empowerment, and revenue growth. Notably, interaction effects showed that these associations were significantly strengthened following the training. Additional results reveal that, after the training, firms not only adopted a greater number of AI business applications but also used them more frequently. These behaviours were found to be associated with improvements in business outcomes. The study demonstrates how innovative educational interventions can support entrepreneurs in developing digital competencies.

title: The Quiet Majority: Political Culture and the Psychology of Silence

detail.title: The Quiet Majority: Political Culture and the Psychology of Silence

detail.abstract: This research paper explores why political silence is so widespread in post-Soviet societies like Uzbekistan, even though these governments present themselves as democracies. I argue that this silence is not simply ignorance, but the product of fear, historical trauma, and state narratives that teach people to equate dissent with danger and loyalty with silence. Drawing on my own experience of political openness in the United States during my FLEX exchange, I contrast that culture of debate with the inherited caution back home. The paper shows how silence is manufactured, through education, patriotism, and generational distrust, but also emphasizes that it is not inevitable. Civic education, storytelling, and even small acts of questioning can begin to break this cycle. For me, democracy is not just about elections or institutions; it is about political culture, courage, and the belief that one’s voice matters. This paper is my attempt to understand that silence, and to imagine how my generation might transform it into speech.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces a general method for computing aggregate fluctuations in economies with private information. Instead of the cross-sectional distribution of agents across individual states, the method uses as a state variable a vector of spline coefficients describing a long history of past individual decision rules. The model is then linearized with respect to that vector. Applying the computational method to a Mirrlees RBC economy with known analytical solution recovers the solution perfectly well. This test provides significant confidence on the accuracy of the method.

title: The impact of artificial intelligence on the transformation and optimization of drug launches: How executives from the health industry perceive the ongoing revolution

publicationDetails.journalName: ESCP Business School Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper explores the growing impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on the transformation of drug launch strategies in the French market. In this strictly regulated environment, where pressure regarding lead times and profitability has increased, AI becomes a lever for operational, organizational and strategic change. Based first on a review of extant literature and trends in the French market, and second on data collected during interviews with ten executives from the pharmaceutical industry, this contribution sheds light on what AI can offer in concrete terms: anticipating medical needs, dynamic targeting, medical and economic simulations, real-time management using key smart performance indicators, adaptive scripting of launch processes. It also highlights emerging new models of integrated governance, as well as a cultural shift towards a "learning launch" form of logic. This article identifies technical, human and regulatory barriers to the adoption of AI, and shows that AI does more than optimize existing processes: it brings about a deep redefinition of value-creating conditions in drug launches. France could be a pioneer in this new reference model, at the intersection of data, ethics and health-related innovation.

detail.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to measure how customer relationship (CR) and strategic supplier partnership (SSP) is associated with the financial performance (FP) of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the light of differentiation strategy (DFS) and competitive advantage (CA). Specifically, it examines DFS as a mediator between CR, SSP, and competitive advantage, and CA as a mediator between CR, SSP, DFS, and SMEs’ financial performance. To realise this study, we analysed the data from 155 manufacturing SMEs operating in Kosovo, using structural equation modelling (SEM). The findings show that DFS fully mediates CR – CA and SSP – CA relationships, while CA mediates the links between CR, SSP, and DFS with SMEs’ financial performance. This study provides valuable insights into how DFS and CA interact with supply chain practices, specifically customer and supplier relationships, and how this is linked to stronger SMEs’ financial performance. Thus, it provides practical implications for SME managers by showing that emphasising customer relationships, SSP, and differentiation strategy is associated with stronger financial performance, and contributes to the theoretical development of SCM and strategic management by integrating contingency theory with SC practices through the mediating role of DFS in achieving competitive advantage. We further discuss the implications of these findings and present directions for future research.

title: The Impact of Algorithmic Recommendation on Time Preference: Evidence from Laboratory and Field Experiments
affiliations: York University - Schulich School of Business, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen (CUHK-Shenzhen) and Chinese University of Hong Kong

detail.title: The Impact of Algorithmic Recommendation on Time Preference: Evidence from Laboratory and Field Experiments
detail.abstract: Algorithmic recommendation systems on short video platforms significantly impact young adults' time preferences. Our laboratory and field experiments demonstrate that deactivating personalized recommendations increases patience, with pronounced gender differences: male users become substantially more impatient under algorithmic recommendations while female users remain unaffected. This disparity stems from gendered content consumption patterns, particularly males' preference for high-stimulation content. These findings reveal how digital environments can shape fundamental economic preferences, potentially influencing important life outcomes.

detail.abstract: Many small and medium-sized nonprofits shy away from investing in data management. It's understandable - with tight budgets and pressing program needs, data systems can seem like an expensive luxury. But what if we could change this perspective? Drawing from my hands-on consulting experience, I've developed a straightforward, four-step approach that helps nonprofits get real value from their data without breaking the bank. By focusing on quick wins and gradual improvements, organizations can transform data from a burden into a powerful tool that boosts fundraising, proves impact, and builds sustainability.

title: Techno-Collectivism: Scaling Libertarian Socialist Governance of Digital Infrastructure
affiliations: University of Sydney and Virginia Tech

detail.title: Techno-Collectivism: Scaling Libertarian Socialist Governance of Digital Infrastructure
detail.abstract: Decades of neoliberal capitalism have concentrated power, deepened inequity, and degraded democracy. The global rise of autocracy and the corporate capture of digital infrastructure have entrenched economic and political dominance. Real change is urgent. This paper proposes techno-collectivism: a Chomskyan libertarian socialist model to govern digital infrastructure at scale. By combining communal ownership, needs-based distributive justice, and citizen control, technocollectivism addresses the systemic pathologies of capitalism while avoiding the threat of autocratic capture through scalable coordination. We discuss techno-collectivism's principles and mechanisms, suggesting universities as optimal testbeds for institutional experimentation.

title: Development of a Machine Learning Model for Halal-Compliant Excipient Prediction and Formulation Optimization in Indonesian Pharmaceutical Manufacturing

detail.title: Development of a Machine Learning Model for Halal-Compliant Excipient Prediction and Formulation Optimization in Indonesian Pharmaceutical Manufacturing
detail.abstract: This research presents a novel machine learning (ML) framework designed to accelerate the development of halal-compliant pharmaceuticals in Indonesia. The primary challenge facing Indonesian pharmaceutical manufacturers is the complex and often manual process of identifying and validating halal excipients, which are critical for drug formulation but can be derived from non-halal sources. Our proposed intervention is an ML model that predicts the halal status of excipients by analyzing key features such as their chemical structure, source of origin (e.g., plant, animal, synthetic), and manufacturing process. This model is trained in a curated database of certified halal and non-halal ingredients. We compare this ML-driven approach to the traditional, manual method, which is time-consuming, expensive, and susceptible to human error. The outcome of this research is a validated ML tool that can significantly reduce the time and cost associated with drug formulation, streamline the halal certification process, and ultimately boost the growth and competitiveness of Indonesia's halal pharmaceutical industry.

title: When Data Can’t Flow Upstream: Implications of Restricting API-Generated Data for Model Training
affiliations: City University of Hong Kong (CityU) - Department of Information Systems, Texas Tech University - Rawls College of Business and University of Connecticut - Department of Operations & Information Management

detail.title: When Data Can’t Flow Upstream: Implications of Restricting API-Generated Data for Model Training
detail.abstract: Motivated by the emerging debates and the conflicting realities surrounding whether data generated through Programming Interface (API) offered by AI providers should be permitted for training their foundation models, this study investigates the strategic and welfare consequences of imposing such restrictions. To this end, we develop a game-theoretic model featuring a provider, a developer, and consumers. The provider offers its foundation model through both direct subscriptions to consumers and API licensing to the developer, who builds upon it to provide a differentiated service to consumers. A key feature of the model is the developer’s ability to choose their degree of differentiation from the foundation AI model. We compare two regimes: a regime where the provider can use API-generated data to train its model, and a restricted regime where such usage is prohibited. Our analysis identifies two opposing effects of this restriction: (1) the data constriction effect, which limits data availability and may degrade foundation model quality, and (2) the differentiation enhancement effect, which incentivizes the developer to offer greater product differentiation, expanding the subscription base, supplying more consumer data for training, and thereby improving model quality. The interplay of these effects reveals that restricting the use of API-generated data for foundation model training may paradoxically enhance model performance, particularly when consumers prioritize privacy. Moreover, such a restriction can incentivize both the provider and developer to raise their subscription prices and potentially lead the provider to charge a higher API usage fee. While such a restriction may benefit both the provider and the developer, under certain conditions, despite alleviating privacy concerns, it may harm consumers by raising prices, suppressing foundation model quality, or both. Our findings offer actionable insights for providers, developers, and policymakers navigating data governance in GenAI ecosystems.

title: Paywall Pitfalls: Engagement Costs on the Online User-Generated-Content Platforms
affiliations: Cornell University, Dyson School of Applied Economics and Management, York University - Schulich School of Business and Chinese University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Paywall Pitfalls: Engagement Costs on the Online User-Generated-Content Platforms
detail.abstract: Balancing audience engagement and monetization is a critical challenge in the creator economy. While digital paywalls have proven effective for traditional online publishers, their applicability and effectiveness on user-generated content (UGC) platforms-where individual creators independently implement paywalls-remain unclear. This study investigates the effects of paywall adoption on audience engagement by leveraging granular data from a leading Chinese video-sharing platform. Employing a staggered difference-indifferences approach, we find that the introduction of a paywall significantly reduces overall audience engagement, even with freely accessible content solely. Further analysis reveals differential responses to paywall implementation between paid and never-paid audiences: while paid users exhibit a temporary engagement increase during their subscription period, this effect rapidly dissipates; never-paid users show a sustained decline in engagement, highlighting potential negative spillovers. However, we find that creators who differentiate paywalled content from free offerings-via longer duration or greater topic dissimilarity-can partially mitigate these negative effects. Our findings extend the digital paywall literature by shifting focus to the creator economy and audience-side impacts, providing both theoretical and practical insights for content monetization strategies in competitive UGC environments.
